_why: Step 9 found repository edge source hardened and green under test while
production ran something else entirely: google-auth was never deployed at
all (404 to a feature the client advertises), notion-auth was still the
pre-hardening build minting unsigned bare-UUID OAuth state, and an old
vulnerable spotify-auth was still publicly reachable months after Spotify
left the MVP. Every edge test passed throughout, because they all read the
repository. Nothing anywhere stated what production was SUPPOSED to run.
This file is that statement. `tools/verify-edge-deployment.mjs` checks it
against the live project at release time, and
credentials at all, so an undeclared function cannot be added quietly.
`deploy: false` is a decision, not an omission -- see spotify-auth.

functions.note: Anthropic routine generation. Spends 25 FP through spend_focus_points_v2 and owns the durable idempotency ledger, so it must never be public.
Authenticated sync. Reads the caller's own Notion integration row only.
Provider webhook: the caller is RevenueCat, not a user, so there is no JWT to verify. Authentication is the REVENUECAT_WEBHOOK_SECRET bearer check inside the function.
OAuth start + callback, so it must accept an unauthenticated callback leg. Safety comes from the signed state, the uid binding and the redirect allowlist -- not from verify_jwt.
Same shape as notion-auth. The client lists Google Calendar as an available integration, so production is expected to answer.

OUTSIDE MVP. The deployed build (ezbr_sha256 977309e1...) minted an authorize URL for any redirect_uri it was handed and verified no state, so it was decommissioned in Step 10A rather than hardened. The hardened source is kept here on purpose: deleting it would lose the fix, and re-deploying it needs a rotated client secret plus a product decision, not a redeploy.
